format: Test vectors for the fixed-form statements protocol/identity registers. Each vector's message is the exact bytes signed, as lowercase hex: the prefix, then each field in the order given, each preceded by one 0x00 byte.
algorithm: ML-DSA-65, FIPS 204 ML-DSA.Sign (pure, never HashML-DSA), with an empty context string
signing: FIPS 204's deterministic variant: rnd is 32 zero bytes. What a signer that cannot sign deterministically tests instead is stated in protocol/identity, Fixed-Form Statements
encodings: seed and message lowercase hex; public_key and signature base64url without padding (1,952 and 3,309 bytes decoded); fingerprint the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the decoded public key
seeds: each key is FIPS 204 ML-DSA.KeyGen_internal from a 32-byte seed, the SHA-256 of the ASCII text 'weblisk test vector key ' followed by the key's name
bodies: A vector whose statement signs a digest of a JSON body carries that body, as sent, in body. Its digest field is 'sha256:' and the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical form of body without its signature member, and body's signature is the vector's signature
no_ones_key: Every key here is a vector key. What that means, and what no implementation may do with one, is stated once, in protocol/identity, Fixed-Form Statements

keys.name: identity
keys.plays: an identity key, proving that it holds its key (weblisk/auth/v1) and re-confirming for a destructive act (weblisk/step-up/v1)

keys.name: hub
keys.plays: a hub's first orchestrator key; its fingerprint is the hub_id the credential signs

keys.name: credential
keys.plays: an operator's credential, answering a hub's challenge (weblisk/credential-auth/v1)

keys.name: log-owner-1
keys.plays: a log owner's long-lived key, the log's first authority

keys.name: log-owner-2
keys.plays: the same owner's next long-lived key, the authority after the succession

keys.name: log-key-1
keys.plays: a log key the first authority introduces, which signs checkpoints

keys.name: orchestrator
keys.plays: an orchestrator's current signing key, which signs the service directory it pushes (weblisk/directory/v2)

keys.name: component
keys.plays: a registered component's key, as the pushed directory names it; it signs nothing here

keys.name: holder-1
keys.plays: a person's identity that claims a namespace and signs as its holder (patterns/namespace)

keys.name: holder-1-next
keys.plays: the same person's next key, the incoming key of a rotation

keys.name: holder-2
keys.plays: another person's identity, the incoming holder of a transfer

keys.name: service
keys.plays: a service identity, which a holder may grant publish and which never holds a namespace

vectors.case: an identity answers a service's challenge
a credential answers a hub's challenge; hub_id is the hub key's fingerprint
an identity re-confirms for a destructive act, over the nonce the same token request's credential answers; hub_id is the hub key's fingerprint
the authority introduces a log key; key id is that key's fingerprint
the log key seals the log at entry 42
the outgoing authority hands the log over
the incoming authority takes the log on: the same bytes, its own signature
a person writes a new entry: before and proposal are empty
a person rewrites an entry and the change declares no scope: scope and proposal are empty
a person removes an entry: after, scope and proposal are empty
a person decides to apply a proposal that rewrites an entry
a person decides to apply a proposal that creates an entry: before is empty and proposal is not
a person decides to apply a proposal that removes an entry: after and scope are empty
the orchestrator pushes a component its service directory; digest is sha256: and the SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 form of body without its signature member, and body's signature is this signature
a person claims an unheld namespace at one registry; holder is the claimant's fingerprint and the claim is signed by that key
the holder grants a service identity publish
the holder withdraws that grant: role none
the outgoing holder hands the namespace to another person
the incoming holder takes it on: the same bytes, its own signature
the holder's outgoing key signs a rotation to its incoming key
the holder's incoming key signs the same rotation
the holder retires the namespace: to is empty and only the outgoing holder signs
the holder publishes release 1 at one registry: previous is empty
a publish grantee publishes release 2, naming release 1's index as previous
